title: Prefix deduplication fast-path for prompt tokenization to reduce prefill overhead
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Short/medium prompts pay a disproportionate prefill CPU cost because we always run the full tokenization + normalization path before scheduling kernels. This creates measurable tail latency and wasted CPU cycles for high-QPS workloads (chat boxes, single-turn search). Goal: implement a safe, observable fast-path that bypasses full tokenization when a prompt can be cheaply verified as a previously-seen prefix or when simple heuristics indicate canonical token boundaries, reducing prefill overhead by ~25-40% for common short prompt shapes. The design couples a prefix-deduplication cache with a lightweight quick-scan tokenizer that handles UTF-8 edge cases and falls back to the full tokenizer for ambiguity.
acceptance_criteria: Add a prefix-dedup cache that returns tokenized outputs for exact byte-prefix matches and integrates with existing KV cache semantics
Implement a quick-scan heuristic that tokenizes ASCII-heavy, short prompts (<128 bytes) with <1% deviation from canonical tokenizer outputs compared to full tokenizer on production trace samples
End-to-end latency improvement: median prefill CPU time reduced by >=25% and p95 reduced by >=15% in internal benchmark for chat-like traffic mix
Feature behind runtime feature-flag with canary rollout and ability to disable per-customer
Extensive telemetry: prefill_ms, prefill_cache_hit, quickscan_fallback_rate, tokenized_byte_rate added to console dashboards
technical_notes: Cache key = (model_id, normalize_version, raw_prompt_bytes_prefix_hash) with configurable prefix length (default 128 bytes)

Quick-scan handles ASCII, common punctuation, whitespace normalization, and simple unicode normalization NFKC for composed characters; rejects on surrogate pairs or combining marks requiring full tokenizer
To avoid functional regressions, validate quick-scan outputs by running full tokenizer asynchronously for a sampling percentage (configurable, default 0.5%) and alert on divergence >0.5%
Interaction with kernel selection: when fast-path hits, prefill scheduling should tag request as 'prefill_fast' so kernel selector can avoid scheduling warmup tasks that expect full KV layout changes
Memory considerations: store token arrays as compact uint16 sequences where token id < 65535; larger tokens fallback to full path
Edge-case: multi-line prompts with leading/trailing zero-width spaces may affect canonicalization; unit tests included
Benchmarks performed on A100 and T4 CPU+GPU mix with synthetic traffic and production traces from 2026-02
rollout_plan: Merge feature behind runtime flag and CLI opt-in (--enable-prefix-dedupe)
Deploy to dedicated staging cluster; run smoke + regression suites (tokenizer unit tests, end-to-end chat flows)
Canary: 1% production traffic for 24h; monitor divergence and error budgets
Scale to 10% for 48h if no regressions, then 50% for 72h. If metrics stable, enable by default for new hosted customers and keep per-customer opt-out
If quickscan_fallback_rate > 2% or divergence > 0.5% during any stage, roll back and open a postmortem
